narrative: The model estimated a 67.4% probability that you would fail the bar exam on your first attempt. In practical terms, it judged failure more likely than success, and because your law school application was screened on that risk, it was denied. The strongest reason was your third-year class position: your decile was 2, while accepted students averaged about 5.79. That was the single largest factor pushing the prediction toward failure. Your first-year class position was the second-largest factor: a decile of 2 compared with an accepted average of about 6.00, also increasing the estimated risk. Your undergraduate GPA of 3.70, above the accepted-student average of about 3.23, was the third most important factor; it pushed in the opposite direction, toward passing, but it was not strong enough to outweigh the two class-position signals. The decision therefore reflects a composite risk estimate, not a judgment that you cannot succeed. To improve a future application, consult admissions or academic advising about how to address your low first- and third-year class standing, consider additional coursework or a record of stronger recent grades, and ask whether delaying application, retaking the LSAT if appropriate, or submitting an explanation of your academic trajectory would strengthen your file.
